item.title: Antonian volleyball aims to defend TAPPS Class 6A state championship
item.description: Antonian's Abby Ibarra (17) is embraced by teammates after scoring a point against the Incarnate Word Shamrocks during the second set Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026, at Antonian High School Gym in San Antonio. The Apaches swept the Shamrocks 25-11, 25-17, 25-13. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) One year after ending a championship dry spell, Antonian returns to the TAPPS state volleyball tournament eager for a chance to notch back-to-back titles. The Apaches (45-4) play Tomball Concordia Lutheran (13-19-1) in a Class 6A semifinal at 7 p.m. Friday at Robinson High School. The winner plays the victor of the Fort Worth Nolan and Plano Prestonwood match that precedes it. The title game is set for 4 p.m. Saturday at Robinson. Antonian is one of two local teams at the TAPPS state tournament. Boerne Geneva plays Bryan Brazos Christian in a 4A semifinal on Friday at Waco's McClennan Community College. Antonian returns an experienced team, including five starters from the squad that defeated Dallas Bishop Lynch in four sets in 2025 to win its first TAPPS state championship in eight years and its sixth overall. "From last season to now, we've definitely grown as a team, especially with all the new people that we have," senior middle blocker Maci Cantu said. "Honestly, I feel our chemistry is better than ever and I'm really confident going to state right now." Cantu, senior right side hitter Lucy Rote and sophomore outside hitter Jordyn Daniels return after earning all-tournament honors at state last season. Senior setter Camila Serna and junior outside hitter Abby Ibarra are also back. "State is the end goal and the end result," Serna said. "This team does a lot of hard work and a lot of work behind the scenes that works really well for us." Rote, a fourth-year starter, is especially grateful to be back. She spent most of the latter half of the season nursing a high ankle sprain after rolling it during practice in mid-September. She missed a month as a result. She returned Oct. 15 and has played eight sets in four matches. Because high ankle sprains are notoriously slow to heal, Rote was initially concerned about not being healthy enough to return before season's end. "There was always a little doubt that there was going to be a chance that I wasn't going to be able to come back," Rote said. "That upset me, but doing my rehab and doing my physical therapy was what made me come back so quick. And I came back at a good time. I've been able to practice a little bit and have some games before the state tournament." item.title: Here's where Golden State Valkyries players will play basketball this offseason
item.description: The Valkyries' Gabby Williams drinks champagne at the parade in San Francisco, Nov. 4, 2026. (Douglas Zimmerman/SFGATE) While it's officially the offseason for the Golden State Valkyries , most of the team is doing anything but taking time off from basketball. Top WNBA players often compete year-round, traveling across the world at times to play for teams that can sometimes pay them a higher salary than they make in the league. While there have been domestic ventures aiming to keep players in the United States during the offseason, the fact remains that the grind as a professional women's basketball player hardly stops. But that's good news for the fans who are undoubtedly itching to see their favorite players, and newly minted champions, take the floor again as soon as possible. There are five Valkyries players who plan to remain stateside for Unrivaled , a three-on-three women's basketball league founded by WNBA stars Breanna Stewart and Napheesa Collier, who is rumored to be a free agent target for Golden State . The league plays its regular season on a touring-style schedule throughout different arenas across the country, and two games are even scheduled to take place on Jan. 11 at Chase Center. Gabby Williams is scheduled to play for the Laces (and be joined by her partner, Marine Johannes), Kaitlyn Chen for the Breeze (alongside her former UConn teammate Paige Bueckers), Veronica Burton for the Mist, Tiffany Hayes for the Phantom and Kayla Thornton for the Rose. Kaila Charles is also slated to to play in Unrivaled, though she's one of six in the "player pool" that will be used to help fill in for injuries on other rosters. Then there's the overseas contingency. Rookie Juste Jocyte is signed to compete in the international basketball league startup Project B . The women's league, which has attracted a fair amount of WNBA talent , is scheduled to begin in China in January and to play their games in cities around the world like Tokyo and Valencia, Spain. Cecilia Zandalasini plans to head back home to compete for Italian team Schio . Janelle Salaun, the reigning Sixth Player of the Year and most prominent player to miss the San Francisco parade , is signed up to play for Galatasaray in Turkey. Aminata Gueye signed a deal in June to play for Czech team ZVVZ USK Praha . Development players Ashten Prechtel and Miela Sowah are also both playing internationally. Prechtel is currently competing in Japan for Eneos Sunflowers, which caused her to also miss Wednesday's parade, and Sowah is scheduled to compete in Australia for the Townsville Fire. The three unknowns as of Thursday afternoon are Laeticia Amihere, Kiah Stokes and Iliana Rupert, although Rupert missed this past season because of her pregnancy. item.title: Tottenham chief reveals ultimate aim to win the Premier League as he insists club is on 'right track'
item.description: Tottenham chief executive Vinai Venkatesham believes the club is heading in the right direction again and has outlined an ultimate objective of winning the Premier League . Spurs narrowly avoided a disastrous drop to the Championship during a tumultuous 2025-26 campaign that saw long-standing chairman Daniel Levy leave, while Thomas Frank and Igor Tudor were both sacked before Roberto De Zerbi secured survival on the final day. A summer of heavy spending followed, bringing 10 new signings and several high-profile departures. After a sluggish opening to the campaign, Tottenham travel to Leeds on Saturday on the back of three straight victories. Speaking on The Sports Agents Podcast, Venkatesham said: "We’ve had three better results in a row, but there is nothing here where we think, ‘oh we’ve cracked it’ and we’re right at the start of this journey of where we are going to. Roberto De Zerbi's side have won three games in a row (PA) "There will be good moments this season and bad moments this season, but I firmly believe we’re on the right track to where we want to get to. "Ultimately, I guess the best way to answer your question (about targets) is what are we here for? We’re here to win, right? The people that we’ve attracted to the football club, the long list of people, everyone is here to win. "If you work for Tottenham, when we talk about being here to win, that means we’re here to win the Premier League. That’s what this football club wants to do. It wants to win the Premier League and it wants to be consistent in the Champions League and ultimately win the Champions League. "Can I tell you what year that’s going to happen in? Obviously I can’t but that’s what we’re aiming for and that’s what I want every single person that works for this club to think about every single day." Venkatesham also disclosed that preparing for relegation last season was necessary, stating: "To not make that plan would have been irresponsible." Xavi Simons is set to return to training later this month (Getty) Meanwhile, playmaker Xavi Simons is progressing in his recovery from a severe knee injury and should return to training in late November. The Netherlands international suffered anterior cruciate ligament damage during April's 1-0 victory at Wolves, missing the conclusion of Tottenham's survival battle. ACL injuries typically require a nine-month recovery period, but Simons remains ahead of schedule and is set for first-team contact training later this month after the international break. This opens up the possibility of a match return weeks before the end of the year, delivering a timely boost to De Zerbi.

item.title: Kimi Antonelli opens up on "very emotional" visit to Ayrton Senna's family estate
item.description: Motorsport photo 2026 Formula 1 champion Kimi Antonelli has opened up about his recent visit to Ayrton Senna's family home ahead of this weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix. The Mercedes driver went to Fazenda Dois Lagos, the Senna family estate, on Tuesday, two days after clinching the F1 title in Mexico. He shared a photo of himself sitting in the Lotus 98T that Senna raced in 1986 and thanked the family for an "unforgettable day". Speaking to the media at Interlagos, Antonelli said the experience had been even more emotional than he expected it to be. "I was truly emotional," the Italian said. "A very, very special day, a day that I will remember forever. That's why I will always be thankful and grateful towards the Senna family for allowing me to see that, and to even sit in the car, which was very special. "It was an amazing day. I actually didn't want to leave. I tried to stay as long as I could there, because it was such a nice experience. The Senna family was very open about showing places where Ayrton used to spend most of his time. It was crazy to think. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes "When I was there, I was like, 'Wow, Ayrton was actually here. He was spending time in his room.' It was very emotional and a very, very special day." Antonelli was joined for the visit by his father, Marco, as well as Senna's nephew Bruno and nieces Bianca and Lalalli. Bruno later thanked the 20-year-old on Instagram for "the karting lesson", with the estate having its own kart track. He will also race this weekend with a special tribute helmet to Senna, 35 years since the Brazilian's first home win at Interlagos in 1991. "This one means a lot to me," Antonelli posted on social media alongside the special helmet design. "My special helmet for the weekend! A tribute to my idol and Brazil. I hope you guys like it as much as I do." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.description: Why Alabama’s No. 5 CFP ranking is about to face its biggest test originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The first College Football Playoff rankings created a debate Alabama cannot avoid: How much should one head-to-head result matter when the committee weighs a team’s full season? Alabama opened at No. 5 with a 6-2 record. Tennessee, also 6-2, landed at No. 13 after beating the Crimson Tide by 16 points. LSU is No. 14, also at 6-2, and Alabama visits the Tigers Saturday in a game that could quickly change the playoff conversation. The rankings are not final, and there are several weeks left for teams to improve their résumés. Still, the first reveal puts Alabama in an unusually visible position: a two-loss team ranked in the top five, with a recent head-to-head defeat to another two-loss team ranked eight places lower. The committee says it weighs the whole resume The selection committee says it evaluates a team’s full profile, including schedule strength, head-to-head results, results against common opponents and other relevant factors. Its guidance says head-to-head carries additional consideration when teams are comparable. Let’s Roll! ✊ 📅 Sat. Nov. 7 ⌚️ 2:30 PM CT 📺 ABC https://t.co/zQnD3Ti4d4 — Alabama Football (@AlabamaFTBL) November 5, 2026 That leaves room for debate about what “comparable” means. Alabama’s ranking suggests the committee valued its broader résumé more highly than Tennessee’s victory in their meeting. But the gap is large enough to invite scrutiny, especially with both teams holding identical records. The committee will release another set of rankings next week. LSU is also 6-2 and sits at No. 14. A win would give Alabama another ranked victory to add to its case. A loss would make the Tide’s top-five spot much harder to defend. For LSU, the stakes are just as clear. The Tigers can beat a team the committee currently sees as a playoff contender and strengthen their own position at the same time. The first rankings are a snapshot, not a verdict. But the Alabama-Tennessee gap has made the committee’s criteria part of the story, and Saturday’s game gives both teams a chance to add evidence. item.title: A.J. Brown knee injury ‘raises some concerns’ about Patriots future
item.description: The New England Patriots trading first- and fourth-round draft picks to the Philadelphia Eagles for wide receiver A.J. Brown was a gamble. On the one hand, he was a proven No. 1 wide receiver capable of adding a new level of playmaking ability to what was one of the best offenses in football in 2025. On the other hand, he was heading into his age-29 season off of his least productive season in four years. Eight weeks into the season, the gamble has not paid off. Brown has appeared in just three games so far, catching nine passes for 101 yards. A bigger concern than his output, however, is his injury situation. Not only did he spend four games on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain, he also is currently dealing with a knee injury that has forced him to miss four straight practices and last Sunday’s win in Miami. While that knee injury has not prompted another move to IR, Brown’s short-term availability has been impacted. And beyond that, there are questions about his long-term outlook as well as addressed by ESPN’s Adam Schefter on Thursday morning. “Let’s go back to the offseason, when Philadelphia was shopping A.J. Brown and they were talking to teams,” Schefter said. “One of the reasons that I believe there wasn’t more interest was there were some teams that had some questions about his knee. In fact, when they were advanced discussions for a trade with the Los Angeles Rams that was at one point close to being completed … I think the Rams had some concerns about his knee. The concerns that other teams have had have now manifested themselves in New England this season. “It flared up. … The knee held him out last week, and the knee is threatening to hold him out this week. It’s a knee that I think raises some concerns as to how long he’s going to keep playing here in New England, and producing at a high level.” More Here: pic.twitter.com/qJbKrjlrr4 — Carlos A. Lopez (@LosTalksPats) November 5, 2026 Worries about Brown’s knee are nothing new. Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf himself spoke about them earlier this year. “It’s a factor, but we examined him,” Wolf said back in June. “He’s got a knee that has some wear and tear that we were aware of. Our training staff and medical staff signed off on it.” Regardless of his current availability issues, the Patriots moving on from Brown in the near future is not expected. His contract structure alone would likely prevent such a move from happening: if released next offseason, for example, New England would take on a dead cap charge of almost $26 million. For the time being, though, Brown remains with the Patriots and part of their 53-man roster. How quickly he can return to the field will be seen, though; one line of thinking is that he might be kept out through the team’s trip to Germany next week and into the Week 11 bye to get fully ready for the stretch run. Whether he will be, only time will tell.

item.description: Celtic Board Backs January Spending: Should Defence Come First? Martin O’Neill’s team lost 2-0 at Falkirk on November 1. The damage began in Europe. Cameron Carter-Vickers, usually a reliable pillar, has made errors that cost games, and the back line has looked disorganised. Goalkeeping has become another sore point. O’Neill has rotated between Viljami Sinisalo and Sam Johnstone, and neither has anchored the defence or built consistency. item.description: "We’ve dropped two points" – Kramarić rues late Crystal Palace equaliser Andrej Kramarić was the picture of disgust after TSG Hoffenheim surrendered a lead to draw 1-1 away to Crystal Palace earlier this evening in the Europa League. “We’re disappointed because we played a top-class game," Hoffenheim's Croatian veteran explained in the mixed zone at Selhurst Park afterwards. "We had plenty of chances and were aggressive. The counter-attack that led to the goal for 1-0 was brilliant; after that, we showed what we’re capable of. "I feel sorry for the lads. We deserved three points today. We’ve dropped two points. With lots of young players, we put in a brilliant performance against a Premier League side. "The goals in the final minutes are very frustrating. We showed a lot and were the better side. That’s very positive, but in football, only the result counts. "I had a chance to make it 2-0; we could have scored again, but even a 1-0 win would have been enough. Sometimes it can be a bit like Italian football. "Then we had the numerical advantage. We need to be smarter about that. We’re not satisfied with the point. But playing football like this, we’re a tough team to face. "We wanted the win more. The Premier League is the best league in the world, but we were the better side. It’s good to know that we can hold our own against opponents like that," he added. Detroit Lions special teams coordinator Dave Fipp said Bates' missed 46-yard field goal off the left upright in a win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 1, glanced off holder Jack Fox’s hand. “It was unfortunate,” Fipp said. “No one really knows this, but ultimately the ball ended up kind of hitting Fox's down hand. item.title: Deshaun Watson Gets Bad News as Week 9 Approaches
item.description: Deshaun Watson will be the Cleveland Browns' starter for Week 1. Getty Deshaun Watson’s chances of starting for the Cleveland Browns on Sunday appear to be fading as he remains in concussion protocol ahead of their Week 9 matchup against the New Orleans Saints. Watson missed Thursday’s practice, and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said that Shedeur Sanders is expected to make his first start of the season. Cleveland had not formally ruled Watson out, but head coach Todd Monken made clear Wednesday that a late clearance would present challenges beyond simply getting his quarterback back on the field. Right tackle Tytus Howard cleared concussion protocol in time to play against Pittsburgh despite missing the week’s practices. Monken cautioned against assuming Watson could follow the same path. “I would say it’s a little more difficult for a quarterback than it was for, say, Tytus last week, but we’ll let it play out. But Shedeur, again, he’ll take the reps today with the ones,” Monken said Wednesday. Asked what makes the position different, Monken pointed to the preparation required. “I just mean in terms of the mental aspect of it, just the position itself, I think is much more difficult. If you’re not able to take the team reps and the throwing reps, how do you get the timing with your receivers? I’m just saying it’s very difficult that way.” Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit during Sunday’s 27-6 loss to the Steelers and returned after passing an evaluation. According to the Browns’ statement , he also passed evaluations after the game and Monday morning before reporting Tuesday that symptoms had developed Monday night. item.title: Green Bay Packers seek nominations for FAN Hall of Fame
item.description: The Green Bay Packers will accept nominations for the 29th member of the Packers FAN Hall of Fame until Nov. 30. Fans can nominate themselves, a relative or friend with an essay of 500 words or less describing the merits of the nominee. Each nomination should be accompanied by a photo. Nominations can be made until Nov. 30 at packers.com/FHOF . Fans who do not have internet access can mail nominations to Green Bay Packers FAN Hall of Fame, 330 E. Kilbourn Ave., Suite 1455, Milwaukee WI 53202. With mailed nominations, copies of photos should be included so that originals are not damaged or lost. Ten finalists will be selected in December by the FAN Hall of Fame selection committee. Their profiles will be posted at Packers.com and fans will vote on the finalists during January. The winner will be chosen by the fan vote and the selection committee. The winner will be announced in late February 2027 at Lambeau Field. The winner will receive four club seats to a 2027 Packers home game, four pregame sideline passes, four passes to the Packers Hall of Fame, a custom Packers jersey, a $500 Packers Pro Shop gift certificate, and a one-year subscription to PackersNews.com . Also, their name will be included with other members in the Green Bay Packers Hall of Fame museum at Lambeau Field. The Packers were the first team to create its own hall of fame, which it did in 1967. It added a FAN Hall of Fame selection in 1998. Patrick Suplicki of Stevens Point was the 28th hall of fame members, announced in February. His dad, Elgie, introduced 65-year-old Patrick to the Packers when he was 3. Second time around was a charm for Suplicki, who was a FAN Hall of Fame finalist for 2020. He is one of a couple of winners to be a finalist in previous years.
